title: Lessons 7 9
description: Multiple-choice question bank. Each question has four options and one correct answer.

questions.question: What does reflecting on your work mean?

options.text: Copying another person's work
Thinking about what you did, what you learned, and what could be improved
Deleting your completed work
Changing results to look better

questions.question: Why should you check your work before submitting it?

options.text: To make the file longer
To remove all headings
To find mistakes and make sure it meets the requirements
To avoid completing the task
Information or advice about what was done well and what could be improved
A type of computer virus
A method of deleting files
A spreadsheet chart
Making a project more colourful
Replacing the investigation question
Hiding mistakes
Providing standards or points to check when judging the quality of work

questions.question: What is the final stage to finish an investigation project?

options.text: Collecting the first response
Reviewing the work, reflecting on the outcome, and identifying improvements
Choosing a topic before planning
Creating a blank spreadsheet

questions.question: Why is it good to save earlier versions of your work?

options.text: They make the computer slower on purpose
They prevent all future changes
They let you return to an earlier version if something goes wrong or you need to compare changes
They automatically improve your marks

questions.question: Why is feedback from someone else useful?

options.text: They may notice problems or suggest improvements that you did not notice
It always means your work is incorrect
It removes the need to check your work
It guarantees a perfect result

questions.question: What does it mean to simulate a real place?

options.text: To visit the place in person
To make a photograph of the place
To build an exact copy using real materials
To create a model or virtual version that behaves in a similar way to the real place

questions.question: Which of these is an example of a simulated environment?

options.text: A printed list of names
A flight simulator used to practise flying
A normal classroom desk
A handwritten shopping list

questions.question: A city planner uses a simulation to study traffic during rush hour. Which variable would be most useful to change?

options.text: The colour of the computer keyboard
The planner's favourite food
The number of vehicles or timing of traffic lights
The size of the computer monitor

questions.question: Why might a simulation produce results that differ from real-world events?

options.text: It uses assumptions and simplified models that may not include every real-world factor
It always knows exactly what will happen
It contains every possible detail of reality
It never uses data

questions.question: A farmer uses a simulation to predict crop growth. Which set of variables would provide the most useful information?

options.text: The farmer's clothing and the computer's colour
The number of classroom chairs and desks
The brand of the farmer's phone
Rainfall, temperature, sunlight, soil conditions, and water supply

questions.question: A flood simulation predicts that a town may flood when rainfall exceeds a certain level. What should officials do before using this prediction to make decisions?

options.text: Assume the prediction is always correct
Check the model using reliable data and compare it with real conditions
Ignore the rainfall information
Remove all warning systems

questions.question: A city wants to test new traffic lights before installing them. What should they do?

options.text: Install them everywhere without testing
Ask people to guess the results
Use a traffic simulation to test different timings and traffic conditions
Stop collecting traffic information

questions.question: An architect wants clients to see a building that is not yet built. What is most suitable?

options.text: A 3D computer model or virtual walkthrough of the building
A list of building materials only
A spreadsheet of staff names
A weather report

questions.question: Why are simulations useful for practising rare events?

options.text: They make rare events happen more often in real life
They remove all possible risks permanently
They guarantee that an event will never occur
They allow people to practise safely without waiting for the real event to happen
